_note: Observed failures and the rule each one produces. Injected into every scan prompt. Entry set #1 is from the first PROSPECTOR attempt (2026-08-07).

entries.title: Did the research by hand instead of building the tool
entries.rootCause: Read the spec's 'run the first scan' step literally and skipped the 'stand up the agents' step before it.
entries.rule: Build the machine before running the machine. If you find yourself BEING the engine, stop and go build that part of the engine.

entries.title: Front-loaded infrastructure archaeology and delivered a wall of findings before any conversation
entries.rootCause: Treated an imperative-worded setup section as a blocking checklist.
entries.rule: Setup is plumbing. Do it quietly; report it in one line.

entries.title: Raised an irrelevant environment conflict as a headline decision
entries.rootCause: Confused 'the repo my container booted into' with 'something the operator must decide'.
entries.rule: Don't surface your own environment noise as the operator's problem.

entries.title: Assumed a document's claimed edges were true (gaming markets)
entries.rootCause: Never verified the claimed edge against the operator.
entries.rule: Verify claimed edges before designing around them. Disconfirmed edges are encoded in lib/constraint-filter.mjs, not remembered.

entries.title: Fired multiple-choice questions with no framing
entries.rule: Teach the concept with a real-world analogy, THEN ask. One question at a time. Every time.

entries.title: Every 'consulting rate' source found was an SEO content farm
entries.rootCause: Rate keywords are the most commercially contested search terms on the web, so organic results are almost entirely lead-generation content.
entries.rule: Never cite a rate from a search result. Rates come from signed SOWs, GSA schedules, public procurement records, or nothing. Encoded as SEO_TITLE_PATTERNS / SEO_URL_PATTERNS in lib/source-tiers.mjs.

entries.title: Treated job postings as evidence of consulting demand
entries.rootCause: Job-posting data was the only hard quantitative source available, so it got asked a question it cannot answer.
entries.rule: A job posting is evidence of budget, not of willingness to buy from outside. An org hiring an FTE may be evidence it will NOT hire a consultant. Label this inference, never fact.
